fixes.explanation: Grain is a farmer's kind of gift, baker, so I see how the mix-up happens. But look at who brings what. Cain is the one who brought some of the fruit of the soil (Genesis 4:3). Abel, the shepherd, brought the best portions of the firstborn of his flock (Genesis 4:4). Don't hand Cain's basket to Abel!

Goshen is a real place in Genesis, baker, but it shows up much later (Genesis 47:27). It's not where Cain settles. Genesis 4:16 says he went out from the presence of the LORD and settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden. Right book, different spot on the map, friend!

Adam is Cain's father, baker, and I get why his name jumped out first. He's the big name at the start of the chapter. But the city doesn't take his name. Genesis 4:17 says Cain named it after his son Enoch. If I named a whole city, I'd probably put a cookie stamper on the sign, and nobody would know where to park.

‘Cain's already long gone by then’ implies he has died by the time of Genesis 47:27. The text does not say when Cain died.
‘Wrong map’ calls the baker's answer wrong. ‘I like the confidence’ also assumes the baker feels confident.
‘Cain looked forward to the next generation, not back’ gives a reason for naming the city that the text does not provide.
The joke invents a father for Papa Dorin, adding a family member. Modern jokes about parents are also off limits.
